Commentary.Commentary: That is it from this game and the reigning champions Australia Women start their campaign on a positive note. The action in the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2023 continues on Sunday, the 12th of February with another doubleheader. It is an all-Asian affair as in the first game of the day, India Women will take on arch-rivals Pakistan Women at 6.30 pm IST (1 pm GMT). Then in the second game, Sri Lanka Women square off aginst Bangladesh Women at 10.30 pm IST (5 pm GMT). Both these games will be played at the Newlands in Cape Town and you can join us a lot early for the build-up for both those games. Cheers!

Meg Lanning, the captain of Australia Women says that she is very happy and they came into this game without knowing what to expect in these conditions. Feels that Alyssa Healy and Ellyse Perry batted exceptionally well and adds that she was in the mood and was disappointed to get out. Mentions that with the ball early wickets made all the difference. Tells that Ashleigh Gardner has been bowling quite well for a while and says that she has worked very hard to get to this position.

New Zealand Women skipper, Sophie Devine says that they were really poor in this game in all facets of the game. Tells that Lea Tahuhu was quite good and Amelia Kerr was also outstanding but feels that 170 was always going to be tough. Tells that it was a good effort from them to take wickets at the backend of the innings and feels that they need to learn from this game and be smart in a tournament with a quick turnaround. Tells that they need to figure out the conditions and then take it forward from there and feels that it probably played slower and lower than they expected but reckons that it is all part of the game.

Ashleigh Gardner (3-0-12-5) is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for her brilliant bowling figures. Gardner says that the win was set up by their batters and that gave the bowling unit the flexibility and luxury. Mentions that they started well with the ball and she is just lucky to get wickets in the end. States that she has worked on her wrist position to get up and over the ball to try to turn it. Says that she also tried to bowl fuller in length and says that wickets have been slow and the bounce is bit up and down and reckons that the bowlers need to bowl stump-to-stump line.
The Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Sophie Devine opted to put Australia Women into bat and Lea Tahuhu got them off to a perfect start by dismissing Beth Mooney for a duck. That is the best it got for a while as Meg Lanning and Alyssa Healy put on a big stand. Amelia Kerr did break the stand but Healy got to 50 and Ellyse Perry came out with aggressive intent and went on to score a quickfire 40. Lea Tahuhu picked up three wickets for the Kiwis and so did Amelia Kerr. Australia Women were able to get to 173 which was their best score aginst these opponents. Coming to the chase, it all went wrong up top for New Zealand Women after which they never recovered and Australia Women went on to win comfortably.

New Zealand Women were simply outplayed by Australia Women but a lot of the blame for this surprisingly poor batting display will go to their openers. Sophie Devine and Suzie Bates are one of the most destructive opening pairs in the world and the way they got out in the very first over put the team under pressure. After that, Amelia Kerr just couldn'ty get the ball away and once Bernadine Bezuidenhout fell, the White Ferns lost wickets in a heap. Kerr did hit a flurry of boundaries at one stage but fell soon after and a few boundaries here and there from the tailenders hardly made any difference. New Zealand Women have been dealt a huge blow in terms of net run rate as well and will have to bounce back really strongly in the next game to get their campaign back on track.

Australia Women  had a pretty big total on the board and got off to a perfect start as Megan Schutt knocked over the talismanic opening pair of the White Ferns in the very first over itself. After that the Aussies were always ahead in the game and kept on bowling good line and lengths. This constant pressure brought them regular wickets as well and they managed to bundle out their opponents with 36 balls to spare. Everyone apart from Jess Jonassen and Tahlia McGrath were economical with Ashleigh Gardner being the pick of the bowler with a superb five-wicket haul, her best-ever performance in a T20I game.

A real statement performance this from the reigning champions and Australia Women have simply steamrolled their Trans-Tasman rivals New Zealand Women to start their title-defense in style. It is a big win for the Aussies but it is the heaviest defeat suffered in terms of runs for the White Ferns in T20Is.

OUT! LBW! Ashleigh Gardner gets a five-wicket haul and Australia Women complete a thumping win here in Boland Park! She bowls it quick and touch shorter of fuller length, on off. It turns in sharply and Eden Carson gets stuck in her crease as she tries to work it towards the leg side. The ball hits her pads and Ashleigh Gardner goes up in appeal. The umpire too raises the finger without taking much time and New Zealand Women have been bundled out for just 76! Australia Women win by 97 runs!
A flatter and quicker on off. Eden Carson blocks it out.
Tossed up on middle. Jonas pushes it to long on for a single.
Goes fuller and on middle. Jonas works it towards the leg side.
Fran Jonas is the last batter in for New Zealand Women.

OUT! BOWLED! Ashleigh Gardner gets her fourth wicket and takes the revenge of the six in the previous delivery with some style. Bowls it on the shorter side, pitching on off and turning in. Jess Kerr makes room and tries to cut it but misses and the ball knocks over the stumps.
SIX! Over the fence this time! Tossed up on off. Jess Kerr dances down the track and tonks it over long on for a maximum.
On a length, on off. Kerr makes room and hits it over mid off. The fielder cuts it off inside the fence and the batters run three.
Five dots in this over! Serves it full and on middle. Kerr drives it back to the bowler.
Bowls it short and around off. Kerr leaves it.
Shortish and on off. Kerr slaps it to short mid-wicket.
Goes fuller and on middle. Kerr works it towards the leg side.
On a length, on off. Jess Kerr defends it towards the off side.
A flatter delivery on off. Eden Carson pushes it towards the off side.
WIDE! Short and down the leg side. Carson tries to clip it but misses.
Eden Carson walks out to bat now.

OUT! LBW! Ashleigh Gardner gets her third wicket and it is her second in this over and this has been a pretty poor batting performance from the Kiwis. Pitched on off, touch shorter and it turns into Rowe. She goes back and tries to tuck it towards the leg side but misses it completely. The ball hits her pads and there is a big appeal from Gardner. The umpire raises the finger and though Rowe reviews it, it does not help as there is no bat involved as confirmed by the UltraEdge. The Ball Tracking also shows three reds and Rowe has to walk back.
Goes fuller and on off. Rowe drives it to the cover fielder.
Shorter and on off. Jess Kerr cuts it to to backward point and a single is taken.
On off and quicker. Jess Kerr fends it out.
Jess Kerr is the next batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! THis is getting too easy for Australia Women now! On the shorter side turning into middle at 88 kph. Lea Tahuhu just works it awkwardly towards left of short mid-wicket and Grace Harris takes an easy catch as New Zealand Women lose their seventh.
Commentary.Howout: c Grace Harris b Ashleigh Gardner

Commentary.Commentary: Shorter and on leg. Lea Tahuhu pulls it to fine leg for a single.
Very full and on off. Lea Tahuhu pushes it to covers.
Bangs it short on off. Rowe pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Shorter in length, on off. Lea Tahuhu slaps it to covers for a single.
Oh, nails a yorker this time! On middle and leg and Lea Tahuhu just about manages to get an inside edge onto her pads as she tries to dig it out.
Lea Tahuhu walks in at number 8.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another one bites the dust! Brown comes back into the attack and strikes straightaway. Bowls it full and on middle. Jensen drives it uppishly towards mid on with no timing and power on it and ends up giving an easy catch to Jess Jonassen at mid on. She takes it safely and New Zealand sink further!
Commentary.Howout: c Jess Jonassen b Darcie Brown

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break. This game looks done and dusted at the moment! Australia have buried any hopes New Zealand had coming into this run-chase with regular wickets and the Kiwis have a humongous task of notching up 113 runs from 60 balls now. However, New Zealand need to take this game deep and get as closer to the total as possible as net run-rate could play a big role latter in the tournament. Australia Women, on the other hand, would be looking to seal a big win here and let's see how things pan out from hereon.
FOUR! Alana King keeps bowling it short, Hannah Rowe rocks back and pulls it away in between deep mid-wicket and ;long on for a boundary.
Drags it down around middle, Hayley Jensen flat-bats the pull shot toward deep mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up around off, Hannah Rowe charges down the track and heaves it to wide long on for just another single.
And again! This is shorter and Jensen pulls it toward deep mid-wicket for one more.
Bowls it short and around off, Rowe pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
Quicker and shorter turning away from around off. Hannah Rowe looks to flick but gets a leading edge onto the off side.
Full and outside off, Hannah Rowe steps out and hits it down to long on for a single.
This is floated full and on the stumps, driven down to long on for one.
Shorter one on off, Hayley Jensen keeps it out.
Hayley Jensen is the next batter in.

OUT! BOWLED! Ashleigh Gardner knocks over Amelia Kerr and New Zealand Women are slipping further down. Tosses it up nicely and bowls it nice and full on middle and off. Kerr goes for her favorite sweep shot but misses and the ball takes faint inside edge before cannoning into the stumps. Gardner is elated and Kerr is disappointed with herself.
Quicker and shorter on off, this is cut away straight to the cover region.
Shorter one outside off, Hannah Rowe looks to push at it but gets a leading edge down to long off for a single.
A length ball around off, Kerr looks to cut late but misses.
Good length around off, Amelia Kerr looks to shuffle ans scoop but misses and gets hit on the pads.

FOUR! Great adjustment and Amelia Kerr makes it a hat-yrick of boundaries. Good length outside off, Kerr looks to shuffle across and ramp it over short fine leg but the ball is too wide. Kerr changes the face of the bat and scoops it over short third man for a boundary.
FOUR! Firmly struck and well placed as well. Good length outside off, Amelia Kerr charges towards the ball and hammers it away wide of mid off for another boundary.
FOUR! Good length outside off, Amelia Kerr sees the width and goes after it. Kerr slices it away over backward point for a boundary.
Hannah Rowe walks out to the middle now.

OUT! RUN OUT! In a game of fine margins, New Zealand Women are coming up second best every single time. Tahlia McGrath bowls it a bit shorter an at the stumps. Amelia Kerr walks toward the ball and heaves it to wide long on. They looks for two but there is a bit of stutter from Maddy Green who is running to the danger end. Grace Harris in the deep picks up the ball and fires in a throw toward the bowler. Tahlia McGrath whips off the bails and the replays show that Green's bat was on the line when the bails came off and she has to walk back.
Tahlia McGrath is into the attack now.
A fraction shorter around off, this is forced through mid on for a single.

Risky single! Drifted onto middle and leg, Maddy Green plays it with soft hands toward cover-point and after a bit of hesitation sets off for the single. Jess Jonassen there picks up the ball and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end but Green is safely home.
Two more! Flatter one on leg stump, this is worked off the back foot in front of mid-wicket for a brace.
Full and around off, Maddy Green gets inside the line of the ball and paddles it down to fine leg for a couple of runs.
Dragged down around middle and leg, Amelia Kerr pulls it down to long on for a single.
Alana King starts off with a shorter delivery down leg, Maddy Green fails to take advantage and brooms it to square leg for a single.
Shorter and on the body, Maddy Green gets inside the line and helps it down to fine leg for a single. At the end of the Powerplay, New Zealand Women are reeling at 29/3!
A bit fuller and on middle and leg, Maddy Green flicks it straight to mid-wicket.
On a good length this is nudged away to mid-wicket.
Shorter one over the stumps, Maddy Green pulls it down to deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Maddy Green is the next batter in.

OUT! GONE! Is that a catch? Yes, it is! Darcie Brown and Ellyse Perry are high-fiving eachother but there isn't much interest from anyone else. The third umpire is called in and the soft signal is not out. She checks a couple of different angles and is satisfied that the fingers are underneath the ball and the decision is overturned. Ellyse Perry bangs it in short and over off stump, Bernadine Bezuidenhout looks to club it over mid off but mistimes it badly. Darcie Brown runs forward and puts in the dive just claw the ball just milimeters off the ground. Bezuidenhout cannot believe it as the ball seemed to have half-vollied into the hands and the soft signal was also not out.
Commentary.Howout: c Darcie Brown b Ellyse Perry

Commentary.Commentary: Ellyse Perry starts off with a fuller delivery outside off, shaping it away. Amelia Kerr steps out and jams it out on the off side for a single.
FOUR! This is fine batting from Bezuidenhout. Tossed up on leg stump, Bezuidenhout gets the front leg out of the way and lofts it over wide mid on for a boundary.
On the stumps, Amelia Kerr brings out the reverse sweep now and hits it straight to backward point. They scamper through for one and once again the throw is a poor one, this time at the keeper's end.
A tad shorter around middle and leg, this is swept away to deep square leg for one.

FOUR! Bernadine Bezuidenhout with another boundary and it is a welcome one as well for New Zealand Women. This is flatter and around leg stump, Bezuidenhout plays the reverse sweep and beats backward point to find the fence.
Floated up nice and full around off, this is pushed away toward mid off.
Jess Jonassen starts off with a slower shorter one around off. Amelia Kerr steps out and tucks it to mid-wicket for a quick run. A better throw at the bowler's end and Kerr was a goner.
FOUR! This is banged in short and over middle, Bernadine Bezuidenhout gets on top of the bounce and dpulls it just behind square leg for a boundary.
Amelia Kerr pre-meditates and shuffles right across the stumps. Darcie Brown follows her with a full one, Kerr reverse ramps it down to third man for a single.
Amelia Kerr is trying everything out there but just can't get off strike. A slower short ball this over the stumps, Kerr looks to shuffle across and scoop but is undone by the lack of pace.
Good length on the fisth stump line and swinging away. Amelia Kerr looks to come down the wicket and go downtown but is well beaten.
Amelia Kerr is really struggling to get the ball away at the moment. This is shorter and around off, Kerr chops it back onto the deck.
Digs it in a bit short and around off, Amelia Kerr looks to pull but gets an inside edge.
On a good length around off, this is psuhed away to mid on for a quick single.
Bowls it full and on leg. Kerr tries to clip it but misses. The ball goes off her pads towards the leg side.
Lands it on a length, on off and shapes into Kerr again. Kerr tries to clip it but misses and gets hit on the pads. A half an appeal follows but no damage done.
A tad fuller and on off, this is flicked away to mid-wicket.
On a good lengtnh and at the stumps, kept out by Amelia Kerr.

LEG BYE! Megan Schutt bowls the big inswinger on a good length and shaping back in a long way from outside off. Bernadine Bezuidenhout looks to shuffle acrioss and flick but misses and gets pinged on the pads. The ball rolls on the off side and there's a loud appeal for lbw. The batters scamper through for a leg bye and the throw comes in at the bowler's end. The umpire there tries to get out of the way and falls over but is swift to get back on her feet. Australia Women do review it and it is umpire's call on the impact and hence, the on-field decision stands.
Maiden! Back of a length outside off, Amelia Kerr taps it down toward gully.
Five dots in a row now! Fullish length, pushed well outside off by Darcie Brown and shaping it further away. Yet again Amelia Kerr goes after it but fails to get bat on it.
Full and outside off, swinging away. Keer advances and jams it out toward cover-point.
Good length outside off and shaping further away, Amelia Kerr goes chasing after it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Short and wide outside off, Amelia Kerr slaps it away hard but straight to the fielder at point.
Short of a length around middle and leg, Amelia Kerr looks to tuck but gets an inside edge  onto the thigh pads.
Darcie Brown to start from the other end.
A length ball, swinging in from outside off, Amelia Kerr pushes it away with soft hands wide of backward point for a single. A fascinating first over as 7 runs and two wickets come off it.
Amelia Kerr is the next batter in.

OUT! LBW! What a dream start for Megan Schutt and Australia Women as both the New Zealand Women openers walk back for a duck. Schutt goes a bit wider of the crease and angles in a fullish length delivery from around off stump. Sophie Devine gets across the line and looks to flick it away but instead Devine ends up playing all around it and gets pinged in front. There is a huge appeal and the finger is raised. Devine reviews but there's nothing on UltraEdge and Ball Tracking shows three reds. New Zealand Women in early trouble here.
On a good length again around off, Bernadine Bezuidenhout shuffles and drags it down to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Good length around off, blocked out.
This is pitched up around middle, Bernadine Bezuidenhout blocks it out.
Bernadine Bezuidenhout walks out to the middle now.

OUT! TIMBER! An inventive shot right from the start by Suzie Bates and she pays the ultimate prize. Megan Schutt bowls this one full and on leg stump, Bates shuffles across the stumps and gets down on one knee looking to paddle it away. The ball is just full and Bates gets herself in a tangle as the ball goes on to crash into the stumps. Schutt is elated and Bates departs without scoring.

FIVE WIDES! A real loosener to start with from Megan Schutt as she bowl it on a good length and way down the leg side. Alyssa Healy dives to her left but fails to cut it off and the ball runs away into the fine leg fence. New Zealand Women are up and running.
